Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
summary: Google introduced a Geospatial Reasoning agent combining domain-specific foundation models (WeatherNext, Flood Forecasting, Population Dynamics Foundation Model), spatial tools, and upfront planning to solve complex planetary analysis tasks that standalone LLMs fail at. The agent connects Gemini to Earth AI's capabilities, accepts custom user datasets, and automatically trains predictive models achieving 12% improvement over demographic baselines. Key finding: domain-specific skills plus upfront planning are essential—the full agent significantly outperforms LLM-only and basic-tools baselines on geospatial benchmarks like GeoExpertQueries. Access is expanding via Ask Google Earth and an Agent-to-Agent service for early users.

How Visko streams real-time world models on Google Cloud TPUs
summary: Visko deployed its Orbis live world model—which streams continuously generated video and audio responding to real-time viewer steering—on Google Cloud TPUs in 30 days, achieving 1.07x playback speed on a single TPU slice. The challenge differs fundamentally from offline video generation: each chunk must complete before playback finishes, with strict sequential dependencies and batch size one. Key optimizations included Ulysses context parallelism to distribute token sequences across TPU chips, custom Pallas splash attention kernels, and selective JAX rewrites (audio achieved 5.8x speedup). For builders, the takeaway is that live multimodal inference requires per-step latency optimization rather than throughput maximization, and selective native JAX ports outperform full framework migrations.

Scaling Indic Pretraining: 2.8 Trillion Tokens and an Open Data Generation Pipeline
summary: NVIDIA and AI4Bharat released Nemotron-pretraining-Indic-v1, a 2.8 trillion token synthetic pretraining corpus across 22 Indian constitutional languages, plus an open GPU-accelerated data generation pipeline using NeMo Data Designer and Gemma-4-31B-it. The corpus addresses critical data scarcity for Indic language models, covering native scripts and romanized variants with quality assessment rubrics inspired by MQM standards. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL gained 4.98-9.82 percentage points on five Indic benchmarks after 10 billion Indic tokens of continued pretraining. Developers can load language-specific configurations, adapt prompts for custom domains, and trace outputs to source documents for reproducibility and auditability.

title: Granite Switch 4.1: Chat, Decisions, and Speech from One Endpoint
Welcome Muse Spark Open: open-weight frontier multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta
summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter open-weight multimodal mixture-of-experts model with 42B active parameters per token, designed for agentic coding tasks. The model accepts text, images, audio, and video inputs, features a 1M-token context window, and uses 256 experts per MoE layer with 8 selected per token. For AI engineers, this matters because it offers frontier-class capabilities in an open-weight format with efficient inference through expert routing and multiple deployment options including llama.cpp, vLLM, and SGLang. The key takeaway: use expert parallelism (ep_size) alongside tensor parallelism when deploying or fine-tuning to efficiently distribute the 256 experts across GPUs while keeping memory requirements manageable.

title: Welcome FLUX.3 Image Klein in Diffusers
summary: Black Forest Labs released FLUX.3 Image Klein, an open image generation model available in Hugging Face Diffusers with distilled and base variants. The distilled checkpoint generates 1024×1024 images in 16 steps (~2 seconds on H100), supporting text-to-image, multi-reference image-to-image, and bounding-box layout control. Key features include FP8/NVFP4 quantization for smaller GPUs, DreamBooth LoRA training scripts, and a modular architecture allowing custom pipeline modifications. The model uses Qwen3-VL text encoder, two-stage transformer processing (per-mode then joint blocks), and flow matching for generation. For builders, the main takeaway is the modular design enabling efficient inference optimization—encode prompts once, cache embeddings, and generate multiple images without reloading components.
